title: Magnetic field magnitude
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the magnetic field strength using the Lorentz force and centripetal force relation, yielding B = √3 mv/(2aq).

title: Time in field
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the time spent in the magnetic field, yielding t = (4√3 π a)/(9v).

title: Radius determination
description: Important: Uses the given geometry (projection from (a,0) at 60°, exit perpendicular to y-axis) to correctly determine the radius of the circular path.

title: Angle subtended
description: Important: Correctly identifies the angular displacement of the particle along its circular arc as 120° (or 2π/3 rad).

title: Period calculation
description: Important: Correctly calculates the full period of circular motion T = 2πR/v.

title: Time fraction method
description: Optional: Explicitly states that the time in the field is a fraction of the period: t = (θ/2π)T.

title: Incorrect radius geometry
description: Pitfall: Misinterprets the exit condition or starting geometry, leading to an incorrect radius (e.g., using R = a or R = a/cos60°).

title: Wrong angular displacement
description: Pitfall: Uses an incorrect central angle (e.g., 60°, 90°, or 30°) to calculate the time.

title: Sign or unit error
description: Pitfall: Makes a sign error in the force direction or omits/incorrectly handles units in the final expressions.
